name: Pop-in
meaning: Pops into view with a small bounce
summary: An app icon pops in with a bounce, then a notification badge pops in a moment later.

name: Stagger
meaning: Items appear one after another, slightly offset in time
summary: Chart bars rise one after another from the left, each slightly delayed.

name: Burst
meaning: Lines and dots burst outward as something appears
summary: A like heart fills in, and a ring, lines and dots burst outward at the same moment.

name: Line draw
meaning: A line extends as if it were being drawn
summary: A chart line draws itself on, and is later erased from its starting end.

name: Mask reveal
meaning: Text rises into view from behind an invisible edge
summary: Headline text slides out from behind an invisible edge marked by a single line.

name: Typewriter
meaning: Text appears one character at a time, as if typed
summary: Text is typed into an input field one character at a time, then the send button lights up and is pressed.

name: Count-up
meaning: A number runs up quickly to its final value
summary: A number races upward and locks onto its final value.

name: Kinetic typography
meaning: Words move, scale and turn in time with what is said
summary: Words move the way they mean: one stretches, one bounces, one spins, one slams down.

name: Easing
meaning: Motion speeds up and slows down instead of moving at one speed
summary: Two squares cover the same distance in the same time: the top one at constant speed, the bottom one eased.

name: Overshoot
meaning: Goes a little past the target, then settles back
summary: A gauge needle swings past its target, comes back and settles.

name: Squash & stretch
meaning: Squashes and stretches so that it feels elastic
summary: A bouncing character squashes on landing and stretches as it takes off.

name: Shape morph
meaning: One shape turns smoothly into another
summary: A shape changes smoothly from circle to square to star to heart, with its colour.

name: Liquid motion
meaning: Shapes move and merge like liquid
summary: A blob stretches out, breaks into drops and merges back into one.

name: Motion trail
meaning: A fading trail follows a moving object
summary: A ball moving in a figure eight leaves a fading trail of copies behind it.

name: Particles
meaning: Many small pieces fly out and scatter
summary: Particles keep shooting up from an emitter, spread out and fall.

name: Parallax
meaning: Near and far layers move at different speeds to show depth
summary: A landscape pans sideways; near layers move more and far layers move less, creating depth.

name: Mask transition
meaning: The next scene appears inside a growing shape
summary: A circle- or star-shaped window grows, showing the next scene inside it.

name: Shape transition
meaning: Shapes cover the screen and uncover the next scene
summary: Coloured bands sweep across and cover the frame; when they leave, the next scene is there.

name: Liquid transition
meaning: Liquid flows in and replaces the scene
summary: Paint-like liquid drips down from the top and fills the frame, becoming the next scene.

name: Zoom through
meaning: Zooms into an object and passes through it into the next scene
summary: The camera pushes into the hole of a letter O and comes out in the next scene.

name: Flip
meaning: Turns over like a card to show the other side
summary: A card turns over around its vertical axis and shows its other side.

name: Light sweep
meaning: A band of light crosses a surface
summary: A band of light crosses the surface of a logo badge at an angle.

name: Glitch
meaning: The picture breaks up as if it were malfunctioning
summary: Text slices shift sideways, colours split and small bars appear, with no brightness flashing.

name: Impact shake
meaning: The whole frame shakes when something lands
summary: A heavy headline slab drops with a thud and the whole frame shakes from the impact.

name: Pan
meaning: Pivot the camera left or right
summary: The camera stays in place and pivots from left to right; because it is a rotation, near and far layers slide sideways by the same amount.

name: Tilt
meaning: Pivot the camera up or down
summary: The camera stays in place and pivots upward, from a person at ground level up to the top of a tower.

name: Dolly in
meaning: Move the camera toward the subject
summary: The camera itself moves toward the subject; near objects grow and pass quickly while the distant mountains barely change.

name: Zoom in
meaning: Magnify with the lens (camera stays put)
summary: The camera does not move; only the focal length gets longer, so the whole picture enlarges by the same ratio.

name: Tracking shot
meaning: Move along with the subject
summary: The camera moves sideways at the same speed as a walking person; the person stays centred while nearer posts sweep past faster.

name: Orbit (Arc shot)
meaning: Circle around the subject
summary: The camera travels on a circle around the subject; the person stays centred while the trees and buildings behind sweep sideways.

name: Crane up
meaning: Lift the camera up
summary: The camera rises while tilting down until it looks down on the person.

name: Dolly zoom (Vertigo)
meaning: Subject stays, background warps
summary: The camera pulls back while zooming in by the same ratio; the person keeps the same size and only the background closes in.

name: Rack focus
meaning: Shift focus between near and far
summary: The camera does not move; focus shifts from a flower in the foreground to a person behind it, swapping which one is blurred.

name: Handheld
meaning: A slight shake, as if the camera were held by hand
summary: Adds a small, irregular shake to the whole frame, as if the camera were held by hand instead of on a tripod.

name: FPV drone shot
meaning: Fast, immersive fly-through
summary: A first-person view flying low and fast between two rows of trees, banking from side to side.

name: Dutch angle
meaning: Tilt the frame diagonally
summary: A level camera rolls around its lens axis and holds with the horizon on a diagonal.

name: Slow motion
meaning: Play the action slower
summary: In front of a fixed camera a person rises and falls slowly through a jump while leaves drift down slowly; the whole action is stretched out.

name: Speed ramp
meaning: Change speed mid-shot
summary: Within one shot the playback speed changes smoothly from fast to slow; a graph at bottom left shows the speed.

name: Time-lapse
meaning: Compress hours into seconds
summary: With a fixed camera, 06:00 to 18:00 is compressed into a few seconds; sun, clouds, people and shadows move in fast forward.

name: Freeze frame
meaning: Pause the action for a beat
summary: The picture stops at the moment a jumping person reaches the top, then resumes from the same frame 1.4 s later.

name: Jump cut
meaning: Same framing, skip ahead in time
summary: Camera position and framing stay the same while the person's position and the clock jump; time is skipped inside one scene.

name: Match cut
meaning: Cut on a matching shape or motion
summary: A thrown ball becomes, in the next shot, a sun at the same position and size; two different scenes are joined on a matching shape.

name: Whip pan
meaning: Fast pan blur into the next shot
summary: The camera swings sideways very fast and the next scene is swapped in during the streaked blur.

name: Cross dissolve
meaning: Blend one shot into the next
summary: The next picture is laid over the current one and its opacity rises until it takes over; both show through each other midway.

name: Wipe
meaning: A moving edge replaces the shot
summary: A vertical edge moves from left to right and the next picture replaces the current one behind it.

name: Smash cut
meaning: Abrupt cut to a contrasting scene
summary: A quiet scene of a person asleep cuts with no warning straight to an intense one; the volume meter jumps at the same moment.

name: J-cut
meaning: Next scene's audio starts first
summary: The next scene's audio starts before the picture changes; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.

name: L-cut
meaning: Previous scene's audio carries over
summary: The previous scene's audio carries on for a while after the picture has changed; the picture is shown on top with video and audio timelines below.

name: Modal dialog
meaning: A window opens in the middle while the page behind dims
summary: Clicking "Open" dims the whole page and a small window scales up slightly into the centre; clicking × closes it.

name: Drawer (Off-canvas)
meaning: A menu panel slides in from the side of the screen
summary: Clicking "Menu" slides a tall panel in from the left; clicking outside slides it back.

name: Bottom sheet
meaning: A panel slides up from the bottom of the screen
summary: A finger taps "View details" and a panel rises from the bottom; dragging its handle down closes it.

name: Accordion
meaning: Click a heading to show or hide its content
summary: Clicking the first of three headings opens its content and pushes the rows below down; clicking again closes it.

name: Dropdown (select)
meaning: Click a field to drop a list of options below it
summary: Clicking the field opens four options below it; picking "Nagoya" closes the list and fills the field.

name: Tooltip
meaning: Hover over something to show a short label
summary: Hovering over a "?" icon shows a short note in a dark bubble above it; it disappears when the cursor leaves.

name: Popover
meaning: Click a button to open a small panel pointing at it
summary: Clicking "Details" opens a small white panel to its right with a pointer at the button; clicking OK inside closes it.

name: Toast notification
meaning: A short message appears in a corner and goes away on its own
summary: Clicking "Save" slides a dark notice into the bottom-right corner; when its time bar runs out it slides away.

name: Tabs
meaning: Click a label to switch which panel is shown
summary: Clicking the tabs "Overview, Pricing, Reviews" in turn slides a blue underline across and swaps the content below.

name: Carousel
meaning: Slides that move sideways to show one item at a time
summary: Each click on the right arrow slides a row of three different images one step to the left, and the dot below moves.

name: Toggle switch
meaning: Flip a setting on or off
summary: The switches on the first two of three setting rows are turned on in turn, then off again.

name: Segmented control
meaning: A row of joined buttons that switches the view
summary: Clicking Day, Week or Month slides a blue highlight across and the bar chart below changes height.

name: Filter chips
meaning: Small pills you click to add or remove a filter
summary: Clicking the "New" and "Free" chips adds a check mark and turns them blue, and cards that do not match fade out.

name: Range slider
meaning: Two handles on one track pick a minimum and a maximum
summary: On a price slider, the left handle is dragged right and the right handle left to narrow the range, then both go back.

name: Stepper (+/−)
meaning: Plus and minus buttons that change a number by one
summary: Pressing + three times raises the number from 1 to 4, and pressing − three times brings it back to 1; the number pops on each press.

name: Pagination
meaning: Numbered buttons that move between pages
summary: Clicking 2 and then 3 in the page numbers moves the blue circle and swaps the list above; finally it goes back to 1.

name: Hamburger menu
meaning: A three-line icon that opens the menu
summary: Clicking the three-line icon at the header's right turns it into ×, and a menu drops down from under the header; clicking again closes it.

name: Breadcrumbs
meaning: A trail of links showing where the page sits in the site
summary: Clicking "Courses" in the breadcrumbs goes up to the list page; clicking a card there returns to the detail page.

name: Mega menu
meaning: A wide panel of grouped links that opens from the main menu
summary: Hovering over "Products" in the header drops a full-width panel with three columns of links and an image; it closes when the cursor leaves.

name: Step indicator
meaning: Shows which step of a process you are on
summary: Each click on "Next" turns the next of four step circles into a check and extends the blue line to the following step.

name: Skeleton screen
meaning: Grey shapes stand in for content while it loads
summary: Clicking reload turns the list into grey blocks of the same shape with a sweeping shine; the content returns when loading ends.

name: Spinner
meaning: A spinning circle that means "please wait"
summary: Clicking "Send" washes the card white and a blue arc spins in the middle; when finished it changes to a check and fades.

name: Badge
meaning: A small dot with a number showing a count
summary: Each time a notification arrives, the blue dot on the bell in the header counts up 1, 2, 3; clicking the bell clears it.

name: Empty state
meaning: The screen shown when there is nothing to list yet
summary: Deleting the two list rows with their trash icons brings up an empty-box drawing, "Nothing here yet" and an "Add" button.

name: Parallax scrolling
meaning: On scroll, background layers move slower than the content
summary: As the page scrolls down, the headline moves up normally while the sky and sun, far hills and near hills move more slowly.

name: Fade-in on scroll
meaning: Elements fade in as they scroll into view
summary: As the page scrolls, the heading, the cards and the body text each rise into place and fade in when they enter the view.

name: Sticky header
meaning: The header stays at the top while the page scrolls
summary: The announcement strip scrolls away, but the header below it stops at the top edge and the content scrolls underneath.

name: Pinning
meaning: A section stays fixed while scrolling advances its content
summary: A navy section stops when it fills the view; further scrolling steps the number and photo through 1→2→3, then the section scrolls on.

name: Horizontal scroll
meaning: Scrolling down moves the content sideways
summary: As the page scrolls down, the section holds still and four numbered work cards travel to the left.

name: Scroll snap
meaning: Scrolling settles exactly on the next section
summary: After a small scroll, the page carries itself the rest of the way until the next section's top lines up with the top of the view.

name: Scroll progress bar
meaning: A bar at the top shows how far you have read
summary: As the article is read a bit at a time, the line along the top grows from the left and reaches the far end at the bottom of the page.

name: Highlighter animation
meaning: A highlighter stroke is drawn under key words
summary: As the copy scrolls into view, a yellow highlighter stroke is drawn left to right across the lower half of the key words.

name: Hover lift
meaning: On hover, the element rises with a deeper shadow
summary: Only the card under the cursor lifts slightly and its shadow spreads; it settles back when the cursor leaves.

name: Image zoom on hover
meaning: The photo enlarges inside a fixed frame
summary: The photo under the cursor slowly enlarges while its frame stays the same size, and shrinks back when the cursor leaves.

name: Cursor follower
meaning: A shape trails the mouse pointer with a delay
summary: As the cursor moves around the page, an orange circle follows it a little behind.

name: Magnetic button
meaning: The button is pulled toward a nearby cursor
summary: As the cursor comes near, the button is drawn toward it and follows; when the cursor leaves, the button wobbles back to its place.

name: Ripple effect
meaning: A ripple spreads from the point that was pressed
summary: Each click sends a white circle out from the click point to fill the button, then it fades away.

name: Underline animation
meaning: A link's underline grows from the left on hover
summary: Under the link the cursor is on, an orange line grows from the left; when the cursor leaves, the line shrinks away to the right.

name: Before/after slider
meaning: Drag a divider to compare before and after
summary: Dragging the line in the middle of the photo left and right changes how much of the grey "before" (left) and the coloured "after" (right) is shown.

name: Exit-intent popup
meaning: A popup shown when the visitor is about to leave
summary: When the cursor heads out through the top of the page (toward the tabs and close button), the page dims and a "Wait!" popup opens. The × closes it.

name: Preloader
meaning: A screen shown while the page loads
summary: On a navy screen the number under the logo counts from 0% to 100%; then the screen lifts away and the page underneath fades in.

name: Lazy loading
meaning: Images load only when they come into view
summary: As grey placeholders scroll into view, a spinner turns in each, and the images fade in as they arrive. The top row is loaded from the start.

name: Infinite scroll
meaning: More items load automatically at the bottom
summary: Scrolling down to the end of the list brings up a spinner, then three new items are added so reading can go on.

name: Page transition
meaning: An animation that bridges two pages
summary: Clicking a card in the work list sweeps an orange panel across from the left; the URL changes and the panel exits to the right on the detail page. "Back to list" returns the same way.

name: Smooth scroll
meaning: In-page links glide to their target instead of jumping
summary: Clicking "Pricing" in the menu glides the page down to the pricing section; the up arrow at the bottom right glides it back to the top.

name: Marquee
meaning: Text or logos scroll across in an endless band
summary: Inside a navy band, large service names separated by orange dots keep moving to the left without a gap.

name: Animated gradient
meaning: Background colours keep drifting and blending
summary: Behind the headline, soft patches of orange, light orange, blue and light blue drift in circles and keep blending differently.

name: Floating animation
meaning: Elements bob gently up and down
summary: Next to the headline, a phone, a heart badge and a rating chip each bob gently out of step, and the shadow under the phone grows and shrinks.

name: Backlighting
meaning: The light source sits behind the subject
summary: The sun moves from outside the frame to directly behind the person's head; a thin bright edge appears around the figure, a pale warm haze covers the frame and the side facing the camera darkens.

name: Rim light
meaning: A light from behind that outlines the subject's edge
summary: The surroundings go dark and two lights behind the person, left and right, draw thin bright edges only along both sides of the head and shoulders; the plan at the bottom right shows where the two lights are.

name: Silhouette
meaning: The subject shows as a black shape against a bright sky
summary: As the exposure is set for the bright evening sky, the person, buildings, lamp and tree turn into flat black shapes with no detail and only the sky stays bright.

name: Split lighting
meaning: Light from the side splits the face into lit and dark halves
summary: The light swings from near the front (20°) to directly at the side (90°); the shadow on the head grows from a crescent to exactly half, splitting the face down the middle.

name: Rembrandt lighting
meaning: High side light that leaves a lit triangle on the shadow cheek
summary: A light 45° to the side and 45° up comes on; the right side of the face falls into shadow except for a small inverted triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek.

name: Butterfly lighting
meaning: High frontal light that casts a butterfly shadow under the nose
summary: A light in front of the face and high above comes on; the face lights evenly on both sides and only a small symmetrical shadow falls under the chin.

name: Golden hour
meaning: The low, warm light just after sunrise or before sunset
summary: The sun drops to just above the horizon; sky and ground turn orange, the left side of the person lights up and the shadows of the lamp and tree stretch far to the right.

name: Blue hour
meaning: The time after sunset or before sunrise when the sky turns deep blue
summary: Once the sun has set, the sky turns two bands of deep blue, the windows and street lamp come on in amber and the person becomes a dark blue shape.

name: Bokeh
meaning: Out-of-focus points of light melt into soft discs
summary: As the aperture opens, the in-focus person stays sharp, the buildings behind soften and the street lamps and distant lights spread into large, pale discs.

name: Tilt-shift
meaning: Blur top and bottom so a real scene looks like a miniature
summary: The top and bottom bands of the street blur while only the middle band with the road, the car and the small people stays in focus, so the street looks like a model.

name: Long exposure
meaning: Keep the shutter open long so moving lights become lines
summary: The street turns to night; the moving car fades to almost nothing, a red tail-light line stretches out behind it and white and amber lines run along the opposite lane.

name: Panning shot
meaning: Follow a moving subject so only the background streaks
summary: The camera follows the moving car: the car stays sharp in the middle of the frame while only the buildings, trees and lamps behind it streak sideways.

name: Lens flare
meaning: Rings and spots of light from a bright source in the lens
summary: As the sun comes out from behind a building, rays appear around it and a line of light dots, hexagons and a ring runs from the sun through the centre of the frame to the opposite side.

name: Fisheye lens
meaning: Ultra-wide lens that bulges the centre and bends straight lines
summary: The middle of the street scene bulges out; the vertical lines of the buildings and the lines of the road bow outward while the corners stay where they are.

name: Chromatic aberration
meaning: Red and blue-violet colour fringes along high-contrast edges
summary: The street scene is split into red, green and blue and the three are laid back together at slightly different sizes, so red and cyan fringes appear on the edges of the person, buildings and lamps, larger towards the sides.

name: Vignette
meaning: The corners darken and draw the eye to the centre
summary: The frame darkens smoothly from the corners while the person and the road in the middle stay bright.

name: High-key
meaning: A bright, white-toned image with very light shadows
summary: The landscape and the person turn to light, near-white colours with very faint shadows, and the hump of the histogram at the bottom right moves to the right end.

name: Low-key
meaning: A dark image where only the lit parts stand out
summary: Most of the frame sinks into darkness and the sun goes out; only the right edge of the bust, lit from the side, stays bright. The histogram hump moves to the left end.

name: Black and white
meaning: Remove colour and show brightness only
summary: The colour drains from the same landscape; the sun and the light on the figure turn grey and the shapes read only by their brightness.

name: Duotone
meaning: Show the image in two colours, one for darks and one for lights
summary: The colours of the same landscape are replaced by a range between just two colours: indigo in the darks and pink in the lights.

name: Teal and orange
meaning: Pushes shadows to teal and skin and highlights to orange
summary: In the same landscape the sky, hills, ground and the shadowed figure shift to teal while the sunlit edge of the figure and the sun shift to orange, a complementary contrast.

name: Film grain
meaning: Fine, film-like grain over the image
summary: Fine grain appears over the whole of the same landscape and the colours lean slightly towards a warm cream.

name: Light leak
meaning: Red-orange glow as if light leaked onto the film
summary: From the right edge of the same landscape a band of leaked light comes in, pale yellow on the inside and red at the edge, swaying slowly.

name: Double exposure
meaning: Two photos layered into one frame
summary: The background turns white and the landscape of hills, house, trees and sun appears, scaled down, only inside the shape of the bust.

name: Anticipation
meaning: Pulls back briefly before moving forward
summary: A square character pulls back against its direction of travel, squashes to wind up, then shoots forward.

name: Follow-through
meaning: Parts keep swinging after the body stops
summary: A round character slides in and stops suddenly; only the flag on its head and its tail keep swinging, then settle.

name: Bounce
meaning: Falls and bounces lower until it stops
summary: A ball drops and bounces lower each time until it comes to rest.

name: Wiggle
meaning: Shakes in small, random, continuous jitters
summary: A bell keeps jittering irregularly: not one hit, but a small shake that never stops.

name: Pulse
meaning: Its size throbs like a heartbeat
summary: A heart throbs like a heartbeat, a double beat each time, with rings spreading out.

name: Motion path
meaning: Moves along a curve that you define
summary: A paper plane follows a dotted path, turning as it goes and looping the loop on the way.

name: Ping-pong loop
meaning: Plays forward, then backward, over and over
summary: A square travels to one end, then comes back along the same path as if played in reverse, again and again.

name: Stop-motion style
meaning: Moves in choppy steps, with frames dropped
summary: A star hops across in choppy steps at about 8 frames per second, each frame slightly off.

name: Text scramble
meaning: Letters shuffle at random, then settle
summary: Random characters keep changing, then lock into the right word from left to right.

name: Wave text
meaning: Letters rise and fall in turn, like a wave
summary: The letters of "WAVE TEXT" rise and fall one after another, like a wave.

name: Text on a path
meaning: Text flows along a line or curve
summary: A line of text flows along a wavy line, each letter turning to follow it.

name: Variable font animation
meaning: The weight of the letters changes smoothly
summary: The same word goes smoothly from thin to very bold and back, with a slider below showing the weight.

name: Text mask
meaning: Letters cut out to show a picture inside
summary: Heavy letters are cut out so that a moving seascape shows only inside them; near the end of the cycle the whole picture appears.

name: Repeater
meaning: Duplicates a shape and turns the copies
summary: One shape is duplicated around a circle, and the copies turn and pulse slightly out of step.

name: Kaleidoscope
meaning: Mirrored patterns spread out symmetrically
summary: An 8-way symmetrical pattern turns and spreads out from the centre, like a kaleidoscope.

name: Line boil
meaning: Hand-drawn lines wobble frame to frame
summary: A hand-drawn line picture wobbles every few frames while the picture itself stays still.

name: Push transition
meaning: The next scene pushes the current one out
summary: The next scene slides in from the side and pushes the current one out with it.

name: Blinds transition
meaning: The next scene opens through thin strips
summary: Gaps in a row of thin strips widen until the next scene is fully open.

name: Cube transition
meaning: Changes scenes like a turning cube
summary: Like a turning cube, the front face swings away and the next face comes round.

name: Page curl
meaning: Peels back like paper to show the next page
summary: A page peels back from its corner and folds over, revealing the next page beneath.

name: Pixelate
meaning: Turns into coarse blocks, then switches
summary: The picture turns into coarser and coarser blocks, switches at the coarsest point, then sharpens again.

name: Shatter
meaning: Breaks like glass and the shards fly off
summary: The picture cracks like glass, the shards fly off and the next scene is revealed.

name: Exploded view
meaning: Parts separate to show the structure inside
summary: A phone separates into its layers to show how it is built, then assembles again.

name: Split screen
meaning: Divides the frame to show scenes side by side
summary: One full-frame scene splits into two panels, then three, each with its own scene moving.

name: Timeline on scroll
meaning: A timeline line grows as you scroll
summary: As the page scrolls down, an orange line grows down the timeline; each dot it reaches fills in and its year and event slide in from the right. Scrolling back up reverses it.

name: Scroll text reveal
meaning: Text darkens letter by letter as you scroll
summary: A light gray headline darkens one character at a time from the top left as the page scrolls, and fades back from the end when scrolling up.

name: Stacking cards
meaning: Cards stack on top of each other on scroll
summary: On scroll, the next card rises from below and stacks over the previous one with a small offset; the cards underneath shrink a little and darken.

name: Background color change on scroll
meaning: The page background changes color by section
summary: Each time the scroll moves into a new section, the whole page background blends from cream to navy to light blue; on the dark background the text turns white.

name: Hide-on-scroll header
meaning: Hides on scroll down, returns on scroll up
summary: Scrolling down slides the header up out of view to free the screen; scrolling up even a little brings it straight back.

name: Scrollspy
meaning: Highlights the current section in the menu
summary: As the article scrolls, the table-of-contents item for the section being read lights up, and the highlight moves on when the next heading comes in.

name: Back-to-top button
meaning: Appears lower down and returns you to the top
summary: After scrolling down, a round arrow button appears at the bottom right; clicking it takes the page straight back to the top.

name: Zoom on scroll
meaning: An image grows to fill the screen as you scroll
summary: As the page scrolls, a small photo in the middle grows to fill the window, the text around it fades away and a headline appears over the photo.

name: 3D tilt on hover
meaning: The card tilts in 3D following the cursor
summary: As the cursor moves over the card, the card tilts in depth to match the cursor position and a glare moves across its surface; it settles flat when the cursor leaves.

name: Spotlight hover
meaning: Only the area around the cursor lights up
summary: As the cursor moves over the dark cards, only a circle around it is lit, and the edges of nearby cards glow.

name: Image swap on hover
meaning: Hovering swaps the photo for another shot
summary: With the cursor on a product card, the front photo of the T-shirt cross-fades to a back view; it returns to the front when the cursor leaves.

name: Text roll on hover
meaning: Letters roll up and swap on hover
summary: With the cursor on a menu word, its letters roll up and out one by one while the same word rolls in from below in orange; it rolls back when the cursor leaves.

name: Hover image reveal
meaning: Hovering a list item shows its photo
summary: With the cursor on a row of a text-only list, that row's photo fades in beside the cursor and follows it.

name: Floating label
meaning: The label floats up when you start typing
summary: Clicking the field shrinks the label and moves it onto the top border, leaving the field free for typing; empty and unfocused, the label moves back inside.

name: Inline validation
meaning: Shows right or wrong while you type
summary: While the email address is half typed the field turns red with an "invalid format" message; the moment it is complete it switches to a green check and "OK".

name: Loading button
meaning: Shows loading, then done, inside the button
summary: Clicking the submit button shrinks it to a circle with a spinner inside; when it finishes it widens into a green "Done" with a check.

name: View transition (shared element)
meaning: A list photo expands into the detail page
summary: Clicking a photo in the list grows that same photo into the image at the top of the detail page while the rest changes to the detail page; going back shrinks it into place.

name: Lightbox
meaning: Opens an image large over a dimmed page
summary: Clicking a thumbnail in the gallery dims the page and shows that photo large in the center; the × shrinks it back into its thumbnail.

name: Hotspots
meaning: Dots on an image open notes when clicked
summary: White dots pulse on the product picture; clicking one opens a tooltip about that part, and clicking another dot swaps the tooltip.

name: Countdown timer
meaning: Counts down the time left to a deadline
